label: first copy step (echoed orig(0)) when the first token is r/y/h/d/1/x, long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, where the input is the echoed first original token; 87% of mass), and to a lesser extent at recall_idx 2 (13% of mass). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on the first occurrence of a token. It is strongly selective for the echoed token being r, y, h, d, 1 or x (rate 4-7x baseline, about 80% of mass); other tokens give weaker, sparser activations. Magnitude grows with L: L=9 gives the highest rate, L<=4 almost never fires, L=3 never. Top activations are all recall_idx 1 with r/y/d/x input and L=8-9. The predicate (recall_idx 1, token in set, L>=6) gets dev F1 0.63 and mass recall 0.76. It misses the weaker recall_idx 2 activations and low-magnitude firings on other first tokens, and has many false positives at the same position with small L or low-magnitude cases. Adding a recall_idx 2 clause raised recall but did not improve F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=10: r, y, h, d; t=9: r, y, h, d; t=8: r, y, h, d) and the token being output (most: e, w, g, t, 0, c; least: -, a, 1, p); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9, L=5 & t=6.
